- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or slightly rising, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast growth to 3–5% per period to avoid overcorrection.  
- If official supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is high, model often underestimates upside — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent 7-day average.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts are rising, reverse direction or reduce slope — avoid “bullish bias” in bearish regimes.  
- In multi-event periods (e.g., 20+ auctions), model tends to overfit recent volatility — apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to forecast.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misreads trend — use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.  
- If true outcome is below forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive periods, trigger mean reversion rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per period until trend stabilizes.  
- In high-event periods with net supply negative, model often ignores event impact — add 0.5–1.0% adjustment to forecast based on event count (e.g., 1% per 5 events).
